entries.item: Liveness + header/tech recon on all primary hosts
entries.summary: www.etoro.com (Next.js/Cloudflare), etoropartners.com (WordPress/WP Engine), etorox.com (redirects to www.etoro.com), public-api.etoro.com (Swagger portal) all fingerprinted. No version/stack leaks worth reporting.

entries.item: Public Swagger spec review + embedded demo-credential verification
entries.summary: 163-endpoint public API spec found at public-api.etoro.com/swagger/swagger.json (intentional product feature). "Demo" x-api-key/x-user-key values in the docs tested against /api/v1/me -- returned 401, confirmed non-functional placeholders, not a real leak.

entries.item: delta.app browser-based check (Cloudflare bot-challenge bypass via real Chrome)
entries.summary: delta.app apex is a Webflow-hosted marketing site, not the ReactJS app scope.md implies. Found web.delta.app (real app) is an unlisted subdomain -- confirmed with user to avoid testing it (out of scope).

entries.item: DNS resolution of 189 in-scope *.etoro.com hosts from CT logs
entries.summary: Filtered 226 CT-log candidates down to 189 valid *.etoro.com hosts (excluded etoro.com.cn as a different domain). Resolved CNAME/A records for all; most point to Cloudflare/Akamai/Azure-owned infra as expected.

entries.item: Check for subdomain takeover on dangling CNAMEs
entries.summary: cn.etoro.com CNAME chain dead-ends at a third-party Chinese CDN vendor (ccgslb.com -> lxcvc.com) with no DNS record anywhere -- confirmed via two independent resolvers including the vendor's own authoritative NS. curl to https://cn.etoro.com/ returns HTTP 000 (no connection possible). UPDATE 2026-09-18 17:33 IST: marked 'Not applicable -- Duplicate' by eToro (an earlier May 2026 report beat us to it) -- eToro confirmed the bug is real and a fix is in progress, so the analysis was correct, just not first.
entries.reportRef: Bugcrowd submission c69fc55f-63e3-4996-9226-df1dabcdebe7 (submitted 2026-09-18, CVSS 7.2 High) -- DUPLICATE, no reward -- see evidence/subdomain-takeover-cn/REPORT.md

entries.item: Dev/staging subdomain exposure check
entries.summary: www.dev.etoro.com and www.stg.etoro.com are live but both return 403 (properly access-restricted).

entries.item: Evaluated whether this category could be tested
entries.summary: Decided not to test -- scope.md forbids mass automated tooling, and all resolved *.etoro.com hosts sit behind shared CDN edge IPs (Cloudflare/Akamai/Azure), so port-scanning would hit third-party shared infra, not eToro's origin.

entries.item: .git/.svn exposure, error-page fingerprinting, JS library versions, sourcemaps, TLS cert SANs, OPTIONS methods, Next.js build manifest
entries.summary: No exposed version-control dirs, no verbose error pages, no outdated JS library banners found (bundle is minified), no exposed .js.map files, TLS cert SAN is just the standard etoro.com/*.etoro.com wildcard, TRACE/OPTIONS give no useful gateway fingerprint. Confirmed marketing.etorostatic.com assets are backed by an S3 bucket (infra note only, domain out of listed scope so not probed further).

entries.item: Config/env files, CI/CD files, backup files, swagger docs, directory listing checks
entries.summary: All common sensitive-file paths (.env, web.config, Dockerfile, Jenkinsfile, docker-compose.yml, backup extensions, directory listings) return 403/404 or resolve to the generic Next.js catch-all 404 page. Wayback Machine query attempted but archive.org itself was down at test time.

entries.item: Extracted API/host references from previously-decompiled mobile app sources
entries.summary: Found 10 in-scope *.etoro.com hosts not present in the CT-log list (embed, offlinemode, pages, partners, por, referfriends, site, userstatsapi, go2, billing-pci). Three (embed/referfriends/site) resolve directly to a raw Azure IP with no CDN in front -- verified via TLS cert (valid *.etoro.com DigiCert cert) and IP ownership (Microsoft/Azure) that this is legitimate eToro infra, just a simple redirect service to www.etoro.com. No vulnerability, but expanded the known attack-surface list.

entries.item: Debug/test query parameter probing (?debug=true, ?test=1, ?admin=1)
entries.summary: No behavioral difference from baseline homepage response for any of the three params.

entries.item: Downloaded and analyzed all 18 JS chunks loaded by www.etoro.com homepage
entries.summary: No hardcoded secrets/API keys, no TODO/FIXME comments, no feature-flag objects, no exposed sourcemaps, no service worker, webpack chunk names are hash-based (no leaked route names). Production build is well-minified.

entries.item: Search-engine dorks for exposed docs/.env/log files, leaked credentials on GitHub, bug bounty writeups, exposed Confluence/Jira
entries.summary: Only legitimate public documents indexed (customer agreements, investor reports). No leaked secrets, no indexed .env/log/config files, no public writeups for this specific Bugcrowd program, no indexed internal wiki/Jira. Confirmed builders.etoro.com / api-portal.etoro.com are the official developer portal (matches the public Swagger already found).

entries.item: SPF / DKIM / DMARC records + subdomain-takeover-to-email-trust cross-check
entries.summary: DMARC is strict (p=reject). DKIM selectors (M365, Google Workspace, SendGrid) all valid. SPF uses ~all (soft-fail) but DMARC covers enforcement. Confirmed the cn.etoro.com takeover finding is NOT included in the SPF trust chain, so it can't be used to amplify email spoofing.

entries.item: AXFR zone transfer, DNSSEC, wildcard DNS, NS delegation, CAA record checks
entries.summary: AXFR properly refused on all 4 Akamai nameservers. DNSSEC not implemented and no CAA record set (both low-severity, likely covered by scope.md's TLS-best-practice exclusion). Confirmed *.etoro.com has a wildcard A record (128.251.126.175) that safely redirects any random subdomain to www.etoro.com -- no security impact, informational only.

entries.item: API version enumeration, GraphQL probe, gateway/WAF fingerprint, changelog exposure
entries.summary: public-api.etoro.com returns a blanket 401 on every unauthenticated path except /swagger (explicitly whitelisted). TRACE method disabled (405). No GraphQL endpoint found. No changelog/release-notes exposed.

entries.item: Missing/invalid API key handling + auth bypass via alternate endpoint paths
entries.summary: No key / invalid key / malformed bearer all consistently 401. Path manipulation (internal/ prefix, double-slash, trailing-slash, case variation, URL-encoded space) does not bypass the auth gate.

entries.item: Liveness + header/tech fingerprint on pentest-app.onetrust.com
entries.summary: Live, HTTP/2 200, behind Cloudflare (Turnstile). Angular micro-frontend shell (<mfe-root>), strong security headers present (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Permissions-Policy). Nothing reportable per scope.

entries.item: Downloaded and grepped main/runtime JS bundles for hardcoded secrets, API keys, tokens
entries.summary: All secret/Bearer matches trace to angular-oauth2-oidc library internals (dummyClientSecret, auth header plumbing), not real leaked credentials. No sourcemap exposed. Confirmed stack: Angular + Zone.js + angular-oauth2-oidc for OIDC auth. Only 2 of the app's JS chunks checked so far (micro-frontend loads more lazily) - worth revisiting.

entries.item: CORS misconfiguration check on pentest-app.onetrust.com
entries.summary: Sent Origin: https://evil.com on / and an OPTIONS preflight on /api/. No Access-Control-Allow-Origin reflecting the attacker origin in either response.

entries.item: Probe common config/sensitive file paths (robots.txt, .env, .git/config, app-config.json, etc.)
entries.summary: All 200 responses were the Angular SPA catch-all serving index.html for any unknown path, not real files - avoided false-positive reporting. No sensitive file exposure found.

entries.item: Attempt to identify Lodash/Zone.js pinned versions for CVE check
entries.summary: App is Webpack-based (webpackChunkot_app) with lazy chunks loaded dynamically at navigation time - not enumerable via static grep on main/runtime bundles. Lodash not found in the two bundles checked. Needs a headless-browser crawl (claude-in-chrome) or authenticated session to surface more chunks.

entries.item: Login-flow email enumeration check (browser-driven)
entries.summary: Entered a nonexistent email on the login page; app called POST /api/access/v1/saml-settings/user-type (200) and showed the password step identically to a real-looking email, no distinguishing error. No enumeration observed via UI. Raw response body of that endpoint not yet inspected - worth revisiting once authenticated.

entries.item: Forgot-password flow enumeration/rate-limit check
entries.summary: Flow requires solving an image CAPTCHA before submission. Not attempted - CAPTCHA solving/bypass is out of bounds for this session. Inconclusive, left for user or a future session to test manually.

entries.summary: Wide scope (4/4): ~16 business-asset domains, 4 Android + 4 iOS apps, 1 GitHub org. Mandatory X-Bug-Bounty header on all active traffic - blocked pending user's Bugcrowd username. App credentials need @bugcrowdninja.com signup. Passive recon (crt.sh, GitHub org) can start without blockers.

entries.summary: 208 unique hostnames collected, saved to recon/crtsh_subdomains_raw.txt. Notable: skippayments.com payments cluster (api-payments-secure-*, pci-www, vpn), many 10bis.co.il dev/qa/staging hosts, yourdelivery.de vpnsec hosts, pyszne.pl admin/dev. entries.item: GitHub Actions workflow review + secret scan on github.com/justeattakeaway public repos
entries.method: GitHub API + git clone + grep/git log -p (manual)
entries.summary: 23 public repos. All 6 pull_request_target workflows properly gated (dependabot author/same-repo head, SHA-pinned checkout) - no pwn-request pattern. Cloned 7 smaller repos and grepped tree + full history for AWS/private key/Slack/GitHub/Google tokens and DB strings: no hits (only false positives - Maven wrapper env var, dummy test cert with placeholder password). One low-risk unpinned action (trufflehog@main) noted, not reportable.

entries.item: Decompile + manifest review of Takeaway.com, Just Eat UK, 10bis, Just Eat Israel Android apps
entries.method: adb pull (official Play-installed APKs) + jadx + apktool (manual)
entries.summary: 28 exported components in Takeaway.com. GlobalDeepLinkDispatcherActivity is BROWSABLE with real URL schemes (just-eat-uk://, etc) - 1-click reachable, but routing logic is obfuscated/delegates to Branch SDK - could not confirm a concrete vuln without more RE or dynamic testing. Payment activities exported but only via internal dispatcher:// scheme, not web-reachable. Needs user decision on further investment.

entries.item: Secret/API key scan across 4 decompiled Android apps
entries.summary: No AWS keys/private keys found (one false positive: AWS CRT SDK's generic PEM-builder code). Google Maps API key hardcoded in manifest, identical across Takeaway.com and Just Eat UK - expected practice unless unrestricted (would allow billing abuse) - not tested against Google's APIs without authorization, flagged to user. Branch.io SDK keys found in 10bis are public-by-design, not a leak.

entries.item: SSL pinning bypass + traffic capture on Takeaway.com via Frida + mitmproxy
entries.method: Frida (OkHttp CertificatePinner/TrustManagerImpl hooks) + mitmdump on rooted emulator (manual)
entries.summary: Decrypted uk.api.just-eat.io, features.api.justeattakeaway.com, legal-pages-api-production.je-apis.com traffic. Found hardcoded OAuth client_credentials secret (client_id:secret) sent to auth.just-eat.co.uk/connect/token, confirmed identically in decompiled source (AppConfiguration.kt) across all 12+ country-brand configs. See log-31 for verification attempt and blocker.

entries.item: Attempt to verify impact of hardcoded OAuth client_credentials secret
entries.method: MITM proxy + direct curl + non-intercepting Frida peekBody hook, 3 methods (manual)
entries.summary: All 3 methods (proxy-intercepted, direct curl with X-Bug-Bounty header, and the real un-intercepted app itself) got identical Cloudflare bot-management 403 (cf-mitigated: challenge) on the token endpoint. Did not attempt to defeat the Cloudflare challenge (out of bounds). Secret's hardcoded presence fully confirmed via 2 independent methods; real-world abusability unconfirmed. Needs user decision on report wording before any submission - also surfaced full internal backend endpoint map (jet-external.com, TakeawayPay gateway) as bonus recon.

entries.item: 4th verification attempt via real Chrome browser (claude-in-chrome)
entries.summary: Navigated to auth.just-eat.co.uk directly. Got Cloudflare's auto-JS-challenge, then it escalated to a hard WAF block ('Sorry, you have been blocked') within seconds, likely due to accumulated anomaly signals from all 3 prior attempts on the same IP/session. Stopped - would need to evade the block to go further. Final conclusion: secret's presence fully confirmed (2 methods), real-world abusability genuinely unverifiable due to effective WAF mitigation. Recommending user report as a confirmed secrets-leakage finding with honest framing.

entries.item: Static analysis: characterize what the leaked client_credentials scope actually grants
entries.method: grep + manual code review on decompiled sources (no live requests)
entries.summary: Real user logins use scope 'openid mobile_scope offline_access' - different from the leaked credential's 'consumer_apis' scope. Found KongTokenRequestParams.kt confirming this is a Kong API-gateway service credential (app-to-infrastructure auth), not a user-session token. Known usages (geocode, address autocomplete) are public/anonymous-tier data. Assessed likely severity as P3/P4 range - real finding matching named focus area, but probably not high-impact without evidence of broader access.

entries.item: Submitted report: Hardcoded Kong API-Gateway OAuth2 Client Credentials in Android App
entries.summary: Submitted to target Just-Eat Holding Limited, VRT: Sensitive Data Exposure > Sensitive Data Hardcoded. User reviewed and rewrote the draft themselves before submitting, including the honest caveat that Cloudflare bot-management blocked full impact verification. Pending triage.

entries.item: Triage outcome: Hardcoded Kong API-Gateway OAuth2 Client Credentials report
entries.summary: Closed as Not Applicable - lacked demonstrated impact (credentials/API keys found on a webpage require demonstrated impact per program policy). No reward. This was the exact risk flagged before submission. Program invites resubmission if impact can be shown later.

entries.item: Manifest exported-component review (getdelta) + hardcoded-secret grep (openbook, Google/Firebase key pattern only) + claude-checklist.md backfill
entries.method: manual manifest review + single-purpose grep (no gitleaks/trufflehog installed locally)
entries.summary: getdelta (io.getdelta.android) manifest: all exported=true components are either signature-permission-protected system components or exported by design (deep links, widget config) — no unprotected sensitive component found. openbook Java sources clean for AIza-style hardcoded Google/Firebase keys. openbook's binary manifest still needs an apktool decode pass for the same exported-component review. Backfilled targets/etoro/claude-checklist.md (was missing) from existing testing-log.md/log-1..17 rather than re-running that work.

entries.item: Fixed prior undocumented mitmproxy CA-trust gap; SSL pinning bypass + traffic decryption confirmed working on pentest_rooted AVD
entries.method: frida (ssl-pinning-bypass.js) + mitmproxy CA pushed to /system/etc/security/cacerts on a -writable-system boot
entries.summary: Found an earlier (2026-09-16) dynamic-testing attempt in tools/ that was never logged: mitmproxy handshake failed for every eToro host because the CA was never trusted at system level. Fixed that on the newly-found pentest_rooted AVD and confirmed real TLS decryption works (Braze SDK traffic captured). getdelta's own api.getdelta.io traffic could not be captured — connection stalls under the proxy, likely a TLS-fingerprint-based anti-automation control akin to the DataDome block seen on web; not pursued further as that would be bot-protection evasion.

entries.item: Live invocation test of openbook's exported components (IDnowForegroundService, NetworkStatusReceiver, PreviewActivity)
entries.method: adb am start-service / am broadcast / am start on own rooted test device
entries.summary: Retracted after rigorous re-test: retested from inside a genuine third-party app (com.google.android.contacts, real non-privileged UID, spawned+injected via Frida) instead of adb shell (SYSTEM_UID, exempt from background-service-start limits). startForegroundService() returned null and dumpsys confirmed the service never started. The earlier apparent success was a false positive caused by testing with root/system privilege rather than a real app's privilege. IDnowForegroundService/NetworkStatusReceiver/PreviewActivity exported-component review closed clean for openbook.

entries.item: Re-verified IDnowForegroundService exported-component finding from a genuine non-privileged app process
entries.method: Frida spawn+inject into com.google.android.contacts (real app UID, not adb/root)
entries.summary: Confirmed the earlier apparent finding (log-38) does not hold up: calling startForegroundService() on openbook's exported IDnowForegroundService from inside a genuine unrelated app's own process (not adb shell) returned null and no service started, per Android's background-execution-start restrictions which do not exempt ordinary app UIDs the way they exempt adb shell's SYSTEM_UID. Retracted; closed clean.

entries.item: Root-caused splash-screen hang under MITM proxy on both apps as the known DataDome anti-automation control
entries.method: curl through mitmdump (diagnostic) + relaunching openbook under proxy+Frida, screenshot evidence
entries.summary: getdelta's splash-hang under proxy traced to api.getdelta.io specifically stalling via mitmproxy while a different unrelated host proxied fine at the same time, ruling out local misconfiguration. Relaunching openbook under the same proxy setup produced eToro's literal DataDome block page ('Access is temporarily restricted... Use of developer or inspection tools'), confirming both mobile apps sit behind the same bot-detection control seen on web (2026-09-18). User decided not to attempt a bypass (TLS-fingerprint spoofing etc.), same call as the original DataDome decision. Authenticated/login MITM traffic capture is closed off on both apps for now.

entries.item: Reviewed openbook's full app data directory (shared_prefs, databases, files, no_backup) via rooted pull
entries.method: adb pull /data/data/com.etoro.openbook on pentest_rooted (root), replacing the earlier empty adb backup archives
entries.summary: The 2026-09-18 .ab backup archives were essentially empty (header only). Direct root pull of the full data directory instead: only third-party SDK telemetry (Facebook, Firebase/GMS, AppsFlyer, Urban Airship) and the app's own public feature-flag/config cache found (same class of data as the public web JS bundle review) — no PII or auth secrets, but the app is in an unauthenticated state (DataDome blocks login), so this isn't a meaningful negative result yet. SecureStorage vault present but empty for the same reason. No submittable finding.

entries.item: Cordova wildcard-whitelist (allow-navigation=*, access origin=*) + exposed native JS bridge in com.etoro.openbook, verified with live Chrome DevTools Protocol PoC
entries.method: config.xml review + code trace (CordovaWebViewImpl.onNavigationAttempt) + live PoC via resigned debuggable APK on pentest_rooted, CDP WebSocket
entries.summary: Verified: window._cordovaNative bridge stays attached after same-frame navigation to an arbitrary external origin (confirmed live against wikipedia.org), but a genuine link click opens a separate bridge-less window instead, so real exploitation needs an existing XSS/open-redirect on www.etoro.com content to trigger a same-frame script redirect (none found this session). Also hit an unresolved target-scope mismatch on Bugcrowd's live submission form (com.etoro.openbook not in the target dropdown; com.etoro.etoroplus is a different app, verified via Play Store). User reviewed and decided NOT to submit this finding, given its contingent impact and the open scope question. Kept as a fully documented technical finding for future reference.

entries.item: subfinder enumeration on arc.io
entries.summary: 86 subdomains found. help.arc.io/explorer.arc.io/community.arc.io present but explicitly excluded from testing per program scope.md (ineligible despite matching the *.arc.io wildcard).

entries.item: httpx liveness + tech-detect scan across all 86 discovered subdomains
entries.summary: 35 hosts responded. Most Cloudflare-fronted staging/rpc hosts return 403 behind a Cloudflare Bot Management JS challenge. Identified portal.arc.io (Cloudflare-challenged, likely highest-value Tier B target per reward table), onramp.arc.io/onramp-demo* (live, Next.js), docs.arc.io (live, Vercel) as priority live targets. www.arc.io is Webflow-hosted (low value, SaaS-builder controlled), status.arc.io/pm-bounces.arc.io are third-party SaaS (Atlassian Statuspage / Postmark).

entries.item: Dangling CNAME / subdomain takeover check on non-responding subdomains
entries.method: dig A/CNAME on all 51 subfinder-discovered hosts that gave no httpx response, sanity-checked against a known-live host
entries.summary: All 51 non-responding subdomains are pure NXDOMAIN (no CNAME, no A record) - stale Certificate Transparency log entries with nothing currently provisioned. No dangling-CNAME takeover opportunity found.

entries.item: Browser-based access + JS bundle analysis of portal.arc.io
entries.method: Playwright (system Chrome) to get past Cloudflare bot challenge, then downloaded and grepped all 44 own JS chunks
entries.summary: Confirmed portal.arc.io is the Arc Portal wallet/DeFi UI (Swap, Send, Earn, Agent, Discover) - matches the program's highest-value Tier B example. JS analysis mostly found generic bundled multi-chain wallet-library data (wagmi/viem chain configs); genuinely Arc-specific refs found: api.circle.com, iris-api.circle.com (Circle's CCTP API), api.turnkey.com (wallet key management, ties to in-scope arc-remote-signer repo), and rpc.*.arc.network hostnames (a separate domain from arc.io).

entries.item: subfinder + httpx on arc.network (separate domain discovered via portal.arc.io's JS)
entries.summary: 18 subdomains found. rpc.testnet.arc.network and rpc.drpc.testnet.arc.network (both explicitly in-scope Tier A assets) return 404 on GET / as expected for JSON-RPC endpoints (need POST).

entries.item: JSON-RPC sensitive-method-exposure check on the in-scope testnet RPC endpoints
entries.summary: rpc.testnet.arc.network: all sensitive namespaces (admin_/debug_/personal_/txpool_) correctly return 'method not supported'. Only eth_chainId and web3_clientVersion (no informative leak) work. Clean, good RPC hygiene.

entries.item: Same JSON-RPC exposure check on rpc.drpc.testnet.arc.network
entries.method: curl POST with the same method list
entries.summary: admin_peers correctly blocked. txpool_content blocked by the third-party RPC provider's (dRPC) own commercial tier gating, not an Arc/Circle control. debug_traceTransaction did NOT return 'not supported' - it returned an argument-count error, meaning the debug_ namespace is enabled on this specific provider endpoint. Testnet-only (no real funds at risk), so impact is low per the program's own severity table. Not yet decided whether to report - needs a follow-up call with a real testnet tx hash to see what detail it exposes.

entries.item: debug_traceTransaction follow-up on rpc.drpc.testnet.arc.network with a real testnet tx hash
entries.method: curl POST (eth_blockNumber, eth_getBlockByNumber, debug_traceTransaction with callTracer)
entries.summary: With a valid 2-arg call on a public testnet tx, dRPC returns 'method is not available on free plan' (code 35) - same commercial-tier gate as txpool_content. The earlier arg-count error was just parameter validation before the plan check; debug_ namespace is not actually usable. Downgraded from 'found' to clean, not reportable.

entries.item: arc-remote-signer first pass: signer/enclave gRPC services, public server, default config
entries.method: git clone --depth 1 + manual read (enclave.go, public.go, option.go, configs/app.yaml, docs/architecture.md)
entries.summary: enclave service logic (AES-GCM data-key/key caching, composite cache key) looks sound. Default config binds 0.0.0.0:10340, TLS off, server-only TLS (no client auth), gRPC reflection on, no app-level auth on Sign - but docs state a 1-to-1 validator sidecar model, so this is deployment hardening, not a demonstrable bug (no live instance in scope). Profiler is Datadog outbound push, not an exposed endpoint. crypto/ and keystore packages not yet reviewed.

entries.item: arc-node native_coin_authority precompile (mint/burn/transfer) review
entries.summary: mint/burn/transfer are gated by caller == ALLOWED_CALLER_ADDRESS plus staticcall and delegatecall checks, zero-address/blocklist/zero-amount checks, and checked_add overflow protection on total supply. No unauthorized-mint path found. Rest of precompiles (native_coin_control, system_accounting, call_from, helpers, pq) and contracts/src not yet reviewed.

entries.item: Dependency CVE check on arc-node, arc-remote-signer, malachite lockfiles
entries.method: osv-scanner 2.6.0 (Cargo.lock, package-lock.json, go.mod); output in recon/osv_*.json
entries.summary: Advisories found: arc-node Cargo 25 pkgs, npm 17 pkgs, remote-signer Go 9 pkgs (incl. grpc, x/net), malachite 21 pkgs (libp2p-quic, yamux, quinn-proto, rustls-webpki, hickory-proto, h2). No reachability or PoC established, and scope.md excludes known-vulnerable libraries without a working PoC, so nothing is reportable yet. Network-layer ones are mostly DoS-class (also excluded).

entries.item: arc-node callFrom precompile: sender-spoofing / allowlist review (call_from.rs, evm.rs subcall path, Memo.sol, Multicall3From.sol)
entries.summary: callFrom is only callable by a hardcoded allowlist {MEMO, MULTICALL3_FROM} (CREATE2, zero salt, also in genesis, so no address squatting). evm.rs additionally requires the new sender to be the immediate caller or tx.origin, and rejects static context, value transfers and non-CALL schemes. Both allowlisted contracts pass msg.sender, never a user-supplied sender. No caller-spoofing path to privileged precompiles (native_coin_control/authority) found. native_coin_control caller gate is NATIVE_FIAT_TOKEN_ADDRESS; body beyond the auth checks not yet read.

entries.item: arc-node precompiles: native_coin_control, system_accounting, helpers.rs (balance/transfer/delegatecall helpers)
entries.summary: native_coin_control: caller gate = NATIVE_FIAT_TOKEN, staticcall+delegatecall checks; UNBLOCKLISTED_STATUS=0 matches unset storage so fresh addresses are not blocked. system_accounting: storeGasValues gated to SYSTEM_ADDRESS, ring-buffer stale-read behaviour is documented/intentional. helpers: balance checks, checked_add, selfdestruct guard and journaled writes all sound; no supply/balance mismatch or unauthorized-mint path found. Minor: pack_gas_values doc comment omits nextBaseFee in layout (cosmetic).

entries.item: arc-node Solidity contracts: Denylist, AdminUpgradeableProxy, PermissionedValidatorManager, validator-manager Controller, ValidatorRegistry
entries.method: manual source read + genesis script check (scripts/genesis/ValidatorManager.ts)
entries.summary: Denylist (ERC-7201, initializers disabled, owner not denylistable), AdminUpgradeableProxy (onlyAdmin gate, standard ERC1967) and PVM/Controller/Registry access control are sound. onlyController requires registrationOf != 0 and configureController rejects ID 0, so unassigned callers cannot act on another validator. Registry has no initializer for _nextRegistrationId (defaults to 0), but genesis sets it to validators.length+1 so IDs start at 1; only a hypothetical fresh non-genesis deployment would hit the ID-0/uncontrollable-validator quirk (operational, privileged-role only, not a vuln). Not yet read: ProtocolConfig, protocol-config Controller, common Pausable, ValidatorRegisterer.

entries.item: arc-node: ProtocolConfig (+Controller), Pausable, ValidatorRegisterer contracts; pq / pq-precompile (SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s) precompile
entries.summary: All contracts/src files now reviewed. ProtocolConfig/Controller/Pausable/ValidatorRegisterer: correct onlyController/onlyPauser/onlyOwner gates, ERC-7201 storage, param validation, initializers disabled on impls. Note only: consensus timeouts and blockGasLimit have no upper bound, reachable only by the trusted controller (privileged-role misuse, not a vuln). PQ precompile: selector + strict ABI decode first, base gas 230k + 6/word charged before verification, exact vk(32)/sig(7856) length checks, 200-gas early-revert penalty; no input-validation or metering flaw found.

entries.item: arc-node txpool validator + Denylist enforcement scope (execution-txpool/validator.rs L255-404, execution-validation/denylist.rs, ADR-0005)
entries.summary: Mempool validation fails closed on storage-read errors for both the native blocklist and the Denylist contract, checks sender, `to` and recovered EIP-7702 authorities, and the denylist slot formula matches the Denylist contract's ERC-7201 layout. is_denylisted is used only in the txpool (ADR-0005/CHANGELOG describe it as mempool admission policy, log location=mempool); execution/consensus enforcement is the separate native blocklist precompile path. So a denylisted address is only filtered at mempool admission, by documented design. No demonstrable bug; a block built by a validator that skips the mempool filter is not something testable within scope (no validator access). Remaining in validator.rs: rest of file (L1-255 stateless checks, 1534-line total incl. tests) and consensus.rs not yet read.

entries.item: arc-node block validation: execution-validation/consensus.rs + executor.rs/assembler.rs base-fee (extra_data) chain
entries.summary: Header validation enforces exact 8-byte extra_data, non-zero beneficiary, gas limit and base fee within chainspec bounds, non-decreasing timestamp, and child base fee == decoded parent extra_data. The executor independently recomputes nextBaseFee and rejects a payload whose extra_data differs (executor.rs L243-282); the 'skip if extra_data empty' branch is build-path only, since header validation already rejects empty extra_data. absolute_min_base_fee is 1 on mainnet/testnet/default, so assembler's 'nextBaseFee != 0' condition always holds and cannot cause a self-reject liveness issue. Proposer cannot steer base fee via extra_data. Timestamp future-skew guard is deliberately at CL vote time (documented in code). Not yet read: remainder of txpool validator.rs (L1-255), eth-engine, execution-payload, malachite-app/consensus-db.

entries.summary: 87 subdomains found. Only tether.to, www.tether.to and app.tether.to are in-scope per scope.md; the rest (hadron/alloy/forge/econ/mail/etc. internal infra) are out-of-scope, recorded for mapping only.

entries.item: Liveness + tech-detect on the 3 in-scope hosts
entries.summary: tether.to/www.tether.to: Gatsby 4.25.9 + React static marketing site behind Cloudflare. app.tether.to: AngularJS app behind Cloudflare, redirects to /app/login. Origin IPs hidden behind Cloudflare edge (104.18.16-17.207).

entries.item: SPF/DMARC record check on tether.to
entries.summary: SPF uses hard-fail (-all), DMARC is p=reject with strict DKIM/SPF alignment (adkim=s, aspf=s). Well-configured, no spoofing risk.

entries.item: CORS misconfiguration check on tether.to and app.tether.to
entries.summary: Neither host reflects an arbitrary Origin in Access-Control-Allow-Origin. No CORS misconfiguration found.

entries.item: Sensitive file exposure check (.git/config, .env, security.txt)
entries.summary: .git/config and .env return 403 on both in-scope hosts. tether.to's /.well-known/security.txt returns HTTP 200 but is the Gatsby SPA's HTML catch-all page, not a real file (false positive, same class seen on other targets). No sensitive file exposure.

entries.item: Security headers check on both in-scope hosts
entries.summary: tether.to has a strong header set (CSP frame-ancestors 'none', HSTS, X-Frame-Options deny, nosniff). app.tether.to's session cookie is Secure+HttpOnly with CSP frame-ancestors self. Nothing reportable.

entries.item: Downloaded and analyzed app.tether.to's main bundle + all 28 lazy-loaded Angular webpack chunks
entries.summary: Recovered the app's full same-origin API surface (GET: /account, /balance, /banks, /announcements, /api/v1/int/vasps, /redeem, /logout; POST: /users/signup, /sessions, /password/forgot, /tether/create_acquire, /tether/redeeming, /whitelist/search, etc). No hardcoded secrets/API keys found. No unexpected third-party hosts referenced.

entries.item: Unauthenticated access check on GET /api/v1/int/vasps and other discovered GET endpoints
entries.summary: /api/v1/int/vasps returns 200 unauthenticated with 2,085 entries, but verified this is intentional public Travel-Rule VASP registry reference data (public names + public on-chain DIDs, no PII/user data) - not a finding. All other discovered GET endpoints (/account, /balance, /banks, /announcements, /redeem) correctly 302-redirect to login when unauthenticated. POST endpoints (signup, password reset, sessions, 2FA) deliberately not probed blind/unauthenticated - state-changing, would need a dedicated own-account test plan per Responsible Disclosure Policy.

entries.item: AndroidManifest.xml review - cleartext traffic and network security config
entries.summary: android:usesCleartextTraffic="true" is set app-wide with no network_security_config.xml shipped to scope it down. Means the app will accept plaintext HTTP if a host responds that way, but whether the real production API actually serves over HTTP can't be confirmed statically - would require a live request, which is out of scope (no authorized program for this app). Flagged to user for awareness, not treated as a submittable finding.

entries.item: Backend host + secret discovery from libapp.so (Dart AOT) string extraction
entries.method: strings + grep on libapp.so (manual static review)
entries.summary: Extracted backend hosts: api.farmlokal.com (primary API), api.razorpay.com, d10i8ghbmk7qrh.cloudfront.net (CDN), maps.googleapis.com. Found a Razorpay rzp_live_ key_id and a Google Maps API key, both of which are Razorpay/Google's intended client-embedded public identifiers, not secrets - not findings. No AWS keys, JWT secrets, or other credential material found. Bearer auth scheme string present, consistent with standard bearer-token auth; token storage/refresh logic not traceable further without runtime instrumentation (Dart AOT, no readable source).

entries.item: APK signing cert, allowBackup/debuggable flags, second secret-key pass, plaintext-HTTP usage check
entries.method: apksigner verify + strings/grep on libapp.so (manual static review)
entries.summary: Signing cert DN matches the default Android debug-keystore template (CN=Android, OU=Android, O=Google Inc...) - only the DN field, fingerprint is unique to this build, not confirmed as an actual debug-key signing issue. allowBackup/debuggable not set explicitly (defaults true/false) - non-debuggable so adb backup is blocked on Android 12+, low practical exposure. Found one more Firebase-style API key (client-embedded by design, not a secret). Confirmed no Razorpay sk_live_ secret key is embedded client-side (payment secret correctly kept server-side). No hardcoded http:// URLs found in libapp.so (all https) - downgrades the earlier usesCleartextTraffic=true finding from 'likely exploitable' to 'unused hardening gap'.

entries.item: TLS/SSL config check on both in-scope hosts
entries.summary: Both tether.to and app.tether.to support only TLSv1.2/TLSv1.3, all offered ciphers rated A-grade, valid cert on tether.to (Google Trust Services, expires 2026-12-11). No weak protocol/cipher config found.

entries.item: Directory/file brute-force with a targeted 25-path wordlist, low rate (5 req/s)
entries.summary: app.tether.to: every path correctly 302-redirects to login except robots.txt (standard Disallow: / for all). tether.to: every path (including deliberately-random nonexistent ones) returns 200 - confirmed false positive, Gatsby SPA serves the same catch-all HTML for any route. No hidden path/file found on either host.

entries.item: nuclei CVE/exposure/misconfiguration/tech scan on both in-scope hosts
entries.summary: Only info-level WAF/tech-detect templates fired (Cloudflare on both, Gatsby 4.25.9 on tether.to, Angular/AngularJS on app.tether.to). No CVE or misconfiguration findings. Closes out round 1 of Tether web recon - clean across the board so far; next steps need a user decision on creating a test account to exercise POST-only auth/signup/2FA/withdraw flows, and on mobile-app/smart-contract scope.

entries.item: Subdomain enumeration + prod/non-prod scope split
entries.summary: 81 unique *.playerauctions.com subdomains found. Split into 52 in-scope prod candidates and 29 non-prod/sandbox hosts flagged OUT OF SCOPE per program (non-production excluded). Prod attack surface includes account/user/member auth, payment/securepay/checkout, seller/offer/order APIs, gametools, developer, public-api, toolsadmin.

entries.item: DNS enumeration on apex (records + AXFR)
entries.summary: Cloudflare NS, Outlook MX, SPF present (mx+amazonses+sendgrid+outlook, -all), Mandrill+Google verification TXT, no CAA. AXFR refused by both NS. SPF/DKIM/DMARC reward-ineligible per scope so not pursued. Apex/www behind Cloudflare bot-challenge with strong security headers.

entries.item: JS analysis of developer portal — member/auth endpoint mapping
entries.summary: Mapped real authenticated surface: account.playerauctions.com (login/register/accountCenter) and me.playerauctions.com/member/{messenger,myoffer.aspx,myorder,sellorder,offereditor,sellersetting}. These aspx/member endpoints with likely numeric IDs are the primary IDOR/business-logic targets.

entries.item: seller-api root probe — request-signing scheme detected
entries.summary: seller-api.playerauctions.com returns {code:10001,'Missing X-PA-TIMESTAMP header'} — custom request-signed API (X-PA-TIMESTAMP + likely HMAC sign header). Backend Azure/ASP.NET. Lead for later once authenticated (may replay our own signed requests rather than reverse the signer). Azure App Insights appId GUIDs leaked in request-context header (low).

entries.item: Authenticated session + JWT/auth architecture (own account)
entries.summary: Own test account (user 6519464) session on user-api.playerauctions.com. Access token RS256 JWT 30-min expiry (strong); refresh token HS256 24h. Internal issuer host account.pa.com leaked in JWT (minor). Session expires fast -> need fresh cURL per test window. IDOR batch pending 2nd account + simultaneous fresh cURLs. Earlier support.* cURLs were Zendesk (out of scope), discarded.

entries.item: Subdomain takeover triage on 52 prod hosts
entries.summary: scdn01.playerauctions.com is a dangling CNAME to scdn01.wpc.8f34.edgecastcdn.net (EdgeCast/Edgio) whose whole chain is NXDOMAIN. Assessed NOT a practical takeover: EdgeCast/Edgio is enterprise-only (no self-serve hostname claim) and the platform is defunct, so no attacker can claim it. DNS hygiene/info only, not submittable per program's 'no best-practice-config without exploit' rule. mail/mailtrack SendGrid CNAMEs resolve (active, not dangling); NXDOMAIN names have no dangling CNAME. No exploitable takeover found.

entries.item: CORS misconfiguration check (unauthenticated) on key API/app hosts
entries.summary: No exploitable CORS. public-api.playerauctions.com root returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin:* with NO allow-credentials (by-design public API, not exploitable). No arbitrary-origin reflection on www/user-api/account-api/seller-api/offer-api/order-api/me/account/checkout/paymentapi. Credentialed CORS test on authenticated user-api deferred to the auth batch (arbitrary-origin + allow-credentials would be the real ATO-risk case).

entries.item: Credentialed CORS on authenticated user-api
entries.method: curl evil Origin + Bearer (manual, own account)
entries.summary: GET /api/User/status with Origin: evil-pa-test.com + valid Bearer returned 200 but NO Access-Control-Allow-Origin/allow-credentials reflected. No credentialed CORS / cross-origin read. Clean.

entries.item: Own-account state + member endpoint access
entries.summary: Own new account is restricted: /status shows status:-1, isMemberInfoComplete:false, role 'New user'. /api/User/Notifications, /api/Messages/inbox, /api/Messages/sent, /api/messages/detail all return 403 'suspension'. Likely normal new-account anti-fraud limiting; blocks most single-account member testing until verified/active.

entries.item: orderdetail auth-model anomaly — POTENTIAL missing authentication (FLAGGED, not confirmed)
entries.method: curl auth vs no-auth on NON-EXISTENT id (manual)
entries.summary: POTENTIAL FINDING: /api/orderdetail/999999999 returns 404 both WITH and WITHOUT auth, whereas /api/messages/detail returns 401 unauthenticated. The absence of a 401 on orderdetail suggests authentication may not be enforced there -> possible broken access control / IDOR on private order details. NOT confirmed: confirming needs a real order id, which would access another user's private data (prohibited by program) or an order we own (blocked - account suspended). Stopped per workspace rule 5; awaiting user decision on safe confirmation path.

entries.item: HS256 refresh-token secret strength (offline)
entries.method: python hmac vs 103,979-entry jwt.secrets.list (offline, own token)
entries.summary: Our own account's HS256 refresh token signature was tested offline against 61 curated + 103,979 wordlist secrets. NOT cracked -> signing secret is strong. No weak-secret token-forgery / ATO vector. (RS256->HS256 alg-confusion on the access token remains untested; needs a single live forged-token request in a browser-capable context.)

entries.item: Wayback param mining -> _next/image + returnUrl leads (browser-required)
entries.summary: Passive mining found /_next/image?url= (Next.js image optimizer, 170 hits - SSRF/open-proxy class) and login returnUrl= (open-redirect class). Could NOT test either: www.playerauctions.com blocks all non-browser clients with Cloudflare bot-challenge (every curl -> 403 'Just a moment'), and cf_clearance is fingerprint-bound so it can't be replayed via curl. Both leads require in-browser testing. Documented for browser-based confirmation.

entries.item: Browser confirmation of _next/image SSRF + returnUrl open-redirect leads
entries.summary: Both leads tested clean by user in-browser: /_next/image?url= did NOT fetch an external webhook.site URL (no SSRF - Next.js domain allowlist enforced), and login returnUrl= did NOT redirect to an external domain (no open redirect - allowlist/same-origin only). Closed.

entries.item: seller-api request-signing scheme mapping
entries.method: curl staged header probing via error messages (manual)
entries.summary: seller-api enforces a staged signed-request contract: X-PA-TIMESTAMP (10-digit seconds, short freshness/anti-replay window -> 10002 'expired' on stale) + X-PA-SIGN (presence-checked) + X-PA-API-KEY (seller-credential-bound). Presence checks enforced in order. Full validation test (garbage sign/key) blocked by safety classifier mid-probe. Practical hunting here needs an approved-seller API key + the client signing secret (in www JS, which is Cloudflare-bot-challenged for non-browser clients) -> path largely closed without seller onboarding. Appears to be a soundly-designed signed API.

entries.summary: Akamai bot-management returned 403 for 98% of requests regardless of actual path existence (confirmed: same word gave 404 via plain curl but 403 via ffuf). Directory brute-force is effectively neutralized on this CDN-fronted host - not a vulnerability, the WAF is working as intended. Stopped to avoid wasting requests; could retry against non-CDN -latest hosts in future.
